steps.title: Owner goes to the all-verses browser (verse replica closed), revokes the editor from the verse card, stays, then re-enters; the editor keeps writing
steps.note: QA-0120's trigger: 'Browse all verses' clears the active verse, which closes the owner's verse replica (navigation_manager handle_verse_replica_lifecycle); the revoke is then issued from the all-verses browser card ('Options for verse QA Basic', viewport.rs) and must reach the editor through the sync thread's publication lease, not the owner's next visit. Confirm is the very next click (two-step confirm, armed 4 s, so wait_s 3); its accessible name is 'Confirm Revoke role grant for <did>' (confirm_button prefixes the arm button's name), which an exact locator must spell out. The click that closes the verse is denied by the host's per-frame scope re-check after it landed; the client treats that as landed (QA-0163 b). The owner stays on the list until 'reenter' (+90 s, over 60 s after the revoke); the step stays open for the 30 s windows anchored on it (QA-0163 c). The editor's refused writes wait for it to read its own demotion (wait_role), so a write is judged refused only once the editor could know; the never-accepted-elsewhere checks need that same gate, so they are never held vacuously. Hierarchy polling is paused (QA-0125).

steps.title: Owner leaves the petal for the verse level, revokes editor2 there, walks back into Swarm Petal; editor2 writes property + transform after the revoke
steps.note: Revoking from inside a petal is impossible: verse Options… is disabled there (QA-0093, QA-0152 c), so the owner first climbs to the verse level (breadcrumb), revokes, then re-opens Swarm Petal. Confirm is the very next action after Revoke (no sleep, no sync offset; wait_s 3): the armed button reverts on its own after 4 s, and its accessible name is 'Confirm Revoke role grant for <did>'. Options/Access/Revoke/Confirm are exact-name locators so a substring fallback can never click the Inspector's 'API Access' tab. Hierarchy polling is paused (QA-0125). The race writes fire the moment the Confirm click is acknowledged (after the owner's commit: one fired earlier could precede the revoke and be a legitimately authorized row every peer keeps); editor2's own app may already refuse them, and that refusal is a race outcome that still lets 13b.e5 and 13c.e2 run, because `needs` on an expect:any action means it ran (QA-0163 d).

steps.title: Owner re-grants editor2 Editor at the verse level; rows editor2 wrote while revoked stay refused, its new writes land
steps.note: QA-0131: the empowerment re-read after a re-grant must not re-admit rows written while the author was unauthorized (13b's race2_rest). The role combo option is the plain label 'editor'; Save role is a two-step confirm whose armed button is named 'Confirm Assign role editor to <did>' (the button text 'Confirm role change' is not its accessible name), so that is the very next click. Each click of the chain needs the one before it: when the Access tab does not list the revoked member (QA-0162) the first click is the one finding and nothing after it is attempted, so the re-grant expectations read 'not exercised', never a false failure.

steps.title: Per-key clock: different keys both survive, the same key agrees, a petal rename flip-flop converges
steps.note: Peers: the owner and editor2 (re-granted in 13c); the editor is revoked since 13a and cannot write. Target N4 (owner-created in step 12, still live). Different keys: each peer sets its own key at the same instant, so both must be present on every peer. Same key: both write clock_same; the winner is max (HLC, author DID), so every peer must agree. QA-0166: only a Manager can rename a petal (entity settings), so the flip-flop is owner A -> B -> A through the petal Options dialog (type replaces the field text); the last rename wins by clock on every peer, read as the petal listed under 'Swarm Fractal/A'. An editor2 race on the name is not expressible: it lacks the Manager role. Hierarchy polling runs here because the rename probe reads it.
